title: NY State Assembly · District 35
area: Queens: East Elmhurst, Corona, LeFrak City, parts of Rego Park, Elmhurst, Jackson Heights, and northern Astoria

context.text: The Democratic, Republican, and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were all canceled after Larinda Hooks was the only candidate to file; she advanced to the general election without appearing on a primary ballot.

summary.text: Larinda Hooks is the incumbent Assembly Member for District 35. A community organizer and civic-association leader who worked at Elmcor Youth & Adult Activities, she won the open seat in 2024 after defeating Hiram Monserrate in the Democratic primary and took office on January 1, 2025. She is unopposed on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot.

background.text: According to her campaign website, Hooks was born and raised in East Elmhurst and Corona, is a graduate of New York City public schools, and is the mother of five children who attended public schools; it says she served as PTA president at Veritas High School and PS 127Q. Her official Assembly biography describes her as a mother of five and a grandmother.

Her campaign website says she has worked for the New York City School Construction Authority and the East Harlem Council for Community Improvement, part of the Acacia Network under the Office for People with Developmental Disabilities. Her official biography describes her work there as aimed at people with developmental disabilities and their families.

Hooks served as president of the Ericsson Street Block Association and then as president of the executive board of the East Elmhurst-Corona Civic Association (EECCA), where, according to her official biography, she advocated on public safety, community engagement, and access to resources.

At Elmcor Youth & Adult Activities, Inc., she was Vice Chairperson of the Board and then Vice President of Older Adult Services and Economic Development, according to her official biography. Her campaign website describes her title as director of Senior Services and Economic Development and says she led the creation of three new senior centers.

Her campaign website lists other civic roles, including deputy director of the Flushing Meadows Soap Box Derby, Girl Scouts troop leader, past vice president of the Frederick Douglas Democratic Association, member of Community Board 3Q, board member of the La Guardia Kiwanis Club, and female Democratic district leader in AD 35.

In 2024 Hooks won the Democratic primary for the open District 35 seat on June 25, defeating Hiram Monserrate 59.1% to 40.4%, and won the November 5 general election with 98.7% of the vote. She succeeded Jeffrion Aubry.

She assumed office on January 1, 2025. For 2025-2026 she is a member of the Aging; Banks; Economic Development, Job Creation, Commerce and Industry; Libraries and Education Technology; Science & Technology; and Transportation committees, along with several legislative caucuses and task forces.
In 2026 she is on the ballot as the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate; the June 23 primaries for both lines were canceled because no other candidate filed.

priorities.text: "My commitment to you is simple: I will listen, I will show up, and I will fight for the resources and opportunities our community deserves. That means supporting our local businesses, advocating for safer streets, expanding access to quality education, and ensuring every voice in our community is heard and valued."

On housing: she says she will "fight to create truly affordable housing for working-class and low-income families, spur additional housing development, protect local residents from eviction and displacement, and focus on infrastructure to stem flooding."
On jobs and economic development: she says she will "demand that any development project in our communities use union labor" and will "fight to raise the minimum wage and address wage theft."

On education: as a former PTA president, she says she will fight to ensure schools are fully funded, expand the community-schools model, and expand access to early-childhood and after-school programs.

On public safety and transportation: she says she supports gun buyback and anti-violence programs, and supports expanding the Fair Fares transit-discount program and increasing funding for trains and buses.

positions.summary: Says she will fight in the Assembly to raise the minimum wage and address wage theft.
positions.quote: In the Assembly, Larinda will fight to raise the minimum wage and address wage theft, an issue that has a particularly devastating impact on immigrant communities.

record.text: Prime sponsor of A08840-A, which prohibits state and local correctional facilities from denying entry to visitors who are menstruating, carrying menstrual products, or using contraceptive devices. The bill passed the Assembly and Senate on June 1 and June 3, 2026, and was returned to the Assembly.

Prime sponsor of A06868, which would increase civil penalties for child-labor-law violations. It passed the Assembly 03/25/2025 but died in the Senate on 01/07/2026 and its enacting clause was stricken on 06/01/2026.

Prime sponsor of A11090, the "automatic utility deferment act," which would require utility providers to suspend termination of service and waive late fees for state employees affected by a state-budget-related payroll freeze. Referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee, where it remains pending.

Prime sponsor of A05489, which would establish mandatory reporting requirements for suspected abuse, mistreatment, or neglect of residents in assisted-living and adult-care facilities. Referred to the Health Committee, where it remains pending.
Prime sponsor of A05299, which would expand the Doctors Across New York program to include dentists. Referred to the Health Committee, where it remains pending.
Serves on the Aging, Banks, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Libraries and Education Technology, Science & Technology, and Transportation committees for the 2025-2026 session.
